title: Tic-Tac-Toe
story: X-O-X on a 3x3 grid. The game every child draws on scrap paper. But programming it teaches grid representation, win detection, turn management, and the minimax concept. Build the full two-player game — then teach the computer to play.
why: Tic-tac-toe teaches 2D grid representation (as Vec or array), pattern-based win checking, and complete game state management.
analogy: A 3x3 tic-tac-toe board is like 8 invisible strings stretched across the grid. Place three X's or O's along any string and you win. Your win checker plucks each string — if all three beads match, the game is over. Clean, symmetrical, satisfying.
try_it: Add a display function that prints the board as a 3x3 grid. Implement a simple AI that blocks opponent wins and takes winning moves. Track game statistics: X wins, O wins, draws. Add input validation — reject moves to occupied cells.
tips: Store the 3x3 grid as a 9-element Vec — index = row*3 + col
There are exactly 8 winning lines — 3 rows, 3 columns, 2 diagonals
Check for winner after every move — no need to check empty boards
common_mistakes: Only checking 3 winning lines instead of all 8
Allowing overwrites of occupied cells — always check cell == ' ' first
Not switching the current player after a valid move
